newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean shares seen gaining on rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Chilean shares seen gaining on rate cut.

text.p: Brokers expected Chilean shares to rise on Thursday night's cut in interest rates, but some said gains would be muted by the fact the market already has the cut largely factored into prices.
The blue-chip IPSA index fell for the third straight day on Thursday, ending down 1.80 percent for the day to 130.87 points.

The Central Bank announced a 25 basis point cut in the interbank rate half an hour after trading closed, surprising the market because in the morning, Central Bank board member Pablo Pinera had said there would be no cut in the near future.

Pinera's comments, made in London, helped drive down prices Thursday. Brokers speculated Friday that the decision to cut rates may not have been taken when he spoke. "What this shows is that Pinera had no idea what was going on. It also shows that the Central Bank is evaluating the performance of the economy every day and that they did not take the decision (to cut rates) a week ago, because then Pinera would have known about it," said a dealer at a major brokerage.
One broker said he expected prices to rise briskly early in the session but then cool off, ending with a slight decline as other bearish factors continued to sway the market.

"I think the market expected a half-point cut," instead of a quarter-of-a-point, he said. "Rates are already at international levels. The market already has this cut factored into prices." Finance Minister Eduardo Aninat praised the Central Bank's measure, which cut the interbank borrowing rate to 6.75 percent annually from 7.000 percent.

"We applaud this measure, which was expected and prudent and in line with a cautious and systematic monetary policy," he said, adding that the rate cut will "encourage better activity indices in the second half of the year" after slow growth in the first half.
